notes.summary: Corrected ordinary CLD foundations: middle PSD domination, signed scalar measures, smooth multiplication, support, and original Artinian weights; strong-cone domination fails.
notes.detailedSummary: Proves the Plucker annihilator obstruction on Lambda^2 R^4, reconstructs the four foundational 369 items on the same ordinary open with q=n-p and r=q-1, repairs printed sign/index/cone problems, and preserves nonreduced integration weights. Imports precisely recorded standard CLD/analytic foundations. The 6561-pair diagnostic is finite evidence, not an analytic proof.
notes.text:
Fix a complete non-Archimedean field K, including trivial valuation, a good separated strict boundaryless pure n-dimensional analytic space X, n≥2, and an ordinary open N. Write D=d'd''. A positive current means a symmetric current nonnegative on middle-positive complementary tests, as in CLD 7.2.1. For T of bidegree (p,p), set q=n-p and r=q-1. Tests for T have type (q,q); tests for D(hT) have type (r,r). All products below are ordinary CLD products.

The primary reference is Chambert-Loir–Ducros, Formes différentielles réelles et courants sur les espaces de Berkovich, arXiv:1204.6277v2. The retained cover says 25 July 2025; the internal title says 29 July 2025, 0h06. The 31 applied primary units were freshly displayed with their complete immediate statements, proofs, and surrounding hypotheses. The entire book was retained, not read page by page. Earlier reports, PASS labels, and ROOT decisions are data, not premises.

CLD 11.1.7 supplies compact neighborhood bases, affinoid neighborhood bases on good spaces, and analytic-domain structures on ordinary opens. CLD 15.7.1–2 supplies canonical calibrated level-n calculus and analytic-domain restriction. CLD 15.2.2–4 proves local differential separation on good separated spaces: separate seminorms by an analytic function, compose its logarithmic norm with a smooth real separator, and extend by zero near its zeros. CLD 6.2.4–8 and 15.2.5–9 supplies compact smooth plateaus and compact scalar density. These inputs require neither reducedness nor nontrivial valuation. No global paracompactness of an arbitrary N is assumed.

Finite nonnegative localization follows directly. Cover a compact set by finitely many relatively compact smaller neighborhoods inside the desired charts; choose nonnegative plateaus; divide each plateau by their sum where that sum is positive; multiply by another plateau supported there and equal to one near the compact set. The resulting functions have compact supports in the specified charts and sum to one near the set. Uniform approximation of continuous compact scalars follows from Stone–Weierstrass on the one-point compactification followed by a prescribed-open plateau. This is scalar density, not harmonic regularization.

The essential cone correction is elementary. Put σ_a=(-1)^{a(a-1)/2}. CLD 1.2.6 identifies a symmetric (a,a)-form, written in the convention σ_a ξ_I∧Jξ_J, with a symmetric coefficient matrix on the a-th exterior coefficient space; middle positivity is precisely positive semidefiniteness. For λ=Σ_i d's_i∧d''s_i,
λ^a=a!σ_a Σ_{|I|=a} d's_I∧J(d's_I).
Thus its matrix is a positive scalar multiple of the identity and dominates both signs of every bounded symmetric coefficient matrix. CLD 1.2.11–12 proves preservation of middle positivity under linear pullback and wedge. The coefficient-space dimension is the actual moment-coordinate dimension, not necessarily analytic dimension.

Strong-positive domination is false. On Λ²R⁴ use coordinates 12,13,14,23,24,34. For a decomposable w=a∧b, w∧w=0 gives
P(w)=w12 w34-w13 w24+w14 w23=0.
Consequently L(B)=B12,34-B13,24+B14,23 vanishes on the span of decomposable-square generators of the strong-positive cone. It vanishes on the diagonal matrix representing λ². But for v=e12+e34, L(vvᵗ)=1. Neither cλ²+vvᵗ nor cλ²-vvᵗ can therefore be strongly positive for any c. Middle PSD domination remains valid. This supplies the needed correction to the earlier 367/368 arguments and the printed strong-domination step in CLD 7.2.9. The retained page 162 pixels confirm that wording; CLD 1.2.13 itself asserts only relative interior for the strong cone. No general recognition theorem for arbitrary weakly positive functionals is imported.

The four foundational 369 conclusions follow as follows.

1. SAME-open decomposition. If a compact symmetric (q,q)-form β on N has support inside an ordinary O⊂N, apply CLD 6.5.2 on O itself. Its compact analytic support condition holds because good ordinary domains are almost good. Equivalently, use finite localization and the preceding compact middle-matrix bounds. This gives β=η₊-η₋ with η₊,η₋ middle-positive, compactly supported in O. They extend smoothly by zero to Hausdorff N. Their supports may exceed supp β, but remain inside O. Only the compact constant-majorant argument of CLD 1.10.2 is used; its problematic noncompact majorant wording is unnecessary.

2. Signed scalar measures and multiplication. For every compact diagonal complementary test θ, there is a unique finite signed Radon measure μ(T,θ), supported in supp θ, satisfying ∫f dμ(T,θ)=⟨T,fθ⟩ for compact smooth scalars f. For positive θ this is CLD 7.2.8/11: bound f by its supremum times a plateau, then extend by scalar density and Radon representation. For general θ discard its antisymmetric part and subtract the measures of a middle-positive decomposition. Scalar density proves uniqueness and decomposition independence. Outside supp θ the scalar functional vanishes; density there proves the asserted support even when the decomposition enlarged supports.

Hence ordinary continuous multiplication is uniquely determined by
⟨bT,θ⟩=∫b dμ(T,θ),
with absolute value at most sup_{supp θ}|b| times the total variation of this finite measure. The order-zero current justification uses middle positivity throughout: on each compact chart image, a standard metric power dominates both signs of a bounded coefficient matrix; finite localization bounds the functional in the chart C⁰ test topology. This repairs the printed strong-cone step for the middle-positive T under consideration.

For β=η₊-η₋, η=η₊+η₋, measure uniqueness and positivity give the sharper estimate
|⟨bT,β⟩|≤∫|b| dμ(T,η)≤sup_{supp η}|b|⟨T,η⟩.                 (1)
A plateau equal to one on the compact supports identifies the measure mass with ⟨T,η⟩. For FIXED T, locally uniform b_i→b therefore implies b_iT→bT on every compact test. No changing-current conclusion is inferred.

3. Smooth multiplier. For ordinary smooth g and positive doubly closed T,
D(gT)=Dg∧T.                                                   (2)
For a symmetric compact (r,r)-test α put A=g d''α-d''g∧α, of type (q-1,q). Total-degree Leibniz gives
Dg∧α-gDα=-d'A+C,
C=d'g∧d''α+d''g∧d'α.
The exact identities Jd'=d''J and Jd''=-d'J give JC=-C. Symmetry of T kills C; d'T=0 kills d'A. Signed transposition gives ⟨DS,α⟩=⟨S,Dα⟩, proving (2). Both currents are symmetric, so symmetric tests suffice. Both closedness equations are retained. This directly repairs the complementary indices in printed CLD 8.5.3 and 7.7.5.

4. Defect support. If Z⊂N is ordinary closed and h is continuous, ordinary smooth with Dh=0 off Z, then R=D(hT) is symmetric and supported in Z, by (2), restriction, and CLD 7.1.9. If χ=1 near Z∩supp α, then
⟨R,α⟩=⟨R,χα⟩,                                               (3)
because supp((1-χ)α) misses Z. No positivity or order-zero claim is made for R. The same support conclusion holds if off Z, h is locally a uniform-on-compact limit of ordinary smooth zero-Hessian functions: apply (2), fixed-T multiplication continuity, and transposition locally.

All commutations use TOTAL degrees: moving type (a,b) past type (c,d) gives (-1)^{(a+b)(c+d)}. This follows by permuting exterior generators, consistently with CLD 1.3.3. The different printed exponent in 3.3.10 was checked against page 80 pixels. The d_K appearing in the proof of 3.3.6 must be d_trop, as its statement and argument show. These are explicit algebraic corrections.

The exact analytic support theorem used later is CLD 15.2.1: a type (a,b) G-form on a topologically separated analytic space has support in d_K(x)≥max(a,b), and its support misses a locally Zariski-closed analytic locus of dimension below max(a,b). Ordinary forms are G-forms. Its immediate proof combines d_trop≤d_K from 12.4.2, tropical form vanishing in insufficient dimension from 3.3.6, and analytic dimension theory. Here d_K is graded residual transcendence degree, equal to residual transcendence degree plus rational value-group rank. A projected skeleton dimension is insufficient.

Original integration weights survive. For an Artinian local A, CLD 13.3.4 uses δ_A(B)=length_A(B)/length_A(A). Composition series prove multiplicativity through finite local algebras. CLD 13.3.7 sums local fiber modules and gives calibrated degree λ/μ for generic module length λ and base generic Artinian length μ. Nilreduction has degree 1/μ. CLD 14.4.2 transports calibration with that degree; 15.4.2–3 transports top-form integration. Top-form supports avoid lower-dimensional component intersections, so 16.6.3 yields δ_X=Σ_i m_i δ_{X_i,red}, with the ACTUAL generic lengths m_i. Calibration is independent under appending analytic units by the common-moment construction of 14.3.1–5. No normalization or base extension of arbitrary T is performed. Boundaryless Stokes makes δ_X doubly closed, and it is tautologically BT because hδ_X=[h]. This does not classify arbitrary currents.

notes.summary: Reconstructs all remaining 369 cutoff/dimension results with actual same-open positive tests; finite masses alone give no uniform removability, and the dimension method is empty at r=0.
notes.detailedSummary: Proves weighted cutoff estimates and their exact vanishing criterion, test-specific mass infima and inverse-oscillation lower bounds, ordinary cover localization, removal for dim Z<n-p-1, and the necessary analytic detector bound d_K≥n-p-1. Off-locus regularity and analytic-locus hypotheses remain explicit; the dimensional window supplies no counterexample.
notes.text:
Use the four proved calculus results of n1 on one fixed ordinary open N. T is positive and doubly closed; q=n-p, r=q-1. Z⊂N is ordinary closed; h is continuous and ordinary smooth zero-Hessian off Z. The following six arguments complete the ten-item369 chain.

5. Fix a compact symmetric (r,r)-test α and S=Z∩supp α. For any ordinary neighborhood O of S choose 0≤χ≤1 smooth compact in O and equal to one near S. Decompose ON O itself
D(χα)=η₊-η₋, η=η₊+η₋,
with compact middle-positive η₊,η₋. For smooth g on the SAME N with Dg=0, support localization, transposition, and n1's multiplier identity give
⟨D(hT),α⟩=⟨(h-g)T,D(χα)⟩.
Therefore
|⟨D(hT),α⟩|≤∫|h-g| dμ(T,η)≤sup_{supp η}|h-g|⟨T,η⟩.       (4)
Subtracting g is legitimate because D(gT)=0, although hT need not be closed. These are actual upstairs compact smooth tests whose positive outputs lie inside O. For empty S, use zero cutoff forms.

6. If for each α actual triples (χ_j,η_{j,±},g_j) on the same N make the integral in (4) tend to zero, then the fixed left pairing is zero. Symmetric tests determine the symmetric defect, so D(hT)=0. Vanishing of supremum error times mass is a sufficient stronger condition. The g_j need only approximate h on moving supports. Existence of such triples for an arbitrary original pair is NOT asserted.

7. Let C_{T,α}(S;O) be the infimum of ⟨T,η₊+η₋⟩ over precisely these actual cutoff/decomposition competitors. A competitor exists and has finite mass; positivity makes the infimum nonnegative. It is zero for empty S and nondecreasing as O shrinks. For relatively compact O put ω_g(O)=sup_O|h-g|. Taking the infimum in (4), without assuming attainment, gives
|⟨D(hT),α⟩|≤ω_g(O) C_{T,α}(S;O).                         (5)
If h=g on compact S, continuity supplies relatively compact neighborhoods with arbitrarily small ω_g. Uniformly bounded cutoff masses, or merely a vanishing product in (5), gives removability. Conversely a nonzero detector of magnitude d forces C≥d/ω_g wherever ω_g>0 and forbids ω_g=0. Separate finite masses on each neighborhood do NOT imply uniform small-neighborhood mass control. This infimum is test-specific and is not identified with a standard capacity.

8. If these estimates establish zero on an ordinary cover of a specified W, restriction and finite nonnegative localization of compact tests makes the same defect zero on W. This glues established identities for the original current. It does not create closed approximating currents using a partition. A cover of W does not constitute a basis inside every ordinary open.

9. If Z is locally Zariski closed in analytic domains and dim Z<r=n-p-1, n1's exact CLD support theorem makes every compact (r,r)-test support disjoint from Z. The defect is supported in Z; all pairings vanish. Ordinary localization gives D(hT)=0. The same argument works for ordinary closed Z satisfying d_K(z)<r pointwise. For pure codimension c, the integer condition is c≥p+2. When p=n-1, r=0, so this dimension method removes NO nonempty locus.

10. A nonzero defect has a compact detecting test; symmetrize it. Its support must meet Z, and every point in its support has d_K≥r. Thus a detector meets Z at an ACTUAL analytic point with d_K≥n-p-1. Applying item9 to the original weighted δ_X gives D[h]=0 when dim Z<n-1, retaining generic Artinian weights. This neither recognizes ±h as psh nor constructs separately admissible U,V. For p≥1 the range n-p-1≤dim Z<n-1 is unexcluded by this dimension argument. It does not exhibit a counterexample. For p=0 there is no such dimensional window.

The whole369 paper and proof, its three actual FINAL bodies, and three distinct expanded bodies were examined as different artifacts. The reconstructed chain uses n1's middle-cone, sign, and degree repairs. No universal off-locus regularity, analytic trace, or weighted vanishing follows here merely from D[h]=0.

notes.summary: Repairs complete scalar367/relative368 transfers: initial BT and actual positive doubly closed smooth-factor products are required; hT need not be closed.
notes.detailedSummary: Proves continuous multiplication compatibility via signed coefficient measures, the full graded D(gamma hT) formula and both cross relations, every-open relative transfer, fixed-T scalar nets, and common-chart coefficient limits to smooth factors. An actual torus detector shows a positive scalar can destroy closedness; that current is ineligible for original P21.3.
notes.text:
Use n1's ordinary products and signed coefficient measures. Let F(O)⊂C(O,R) be a restriction-compatible class of finite functions. A positive doubly closed T is BT for F if on EVERY ordinary O, all u,v∈F(O) with D[u]=D[v] satisfy D((u-v)T)=0. Initial BT is an explicit transfer hypothesis. The original individually continuous psh class can be used without replacing it by generated CPsh.

Multiplication compatibility is proved by measures. For smooth β and a complementary compact test ω,
⟨β∧(hT),ω⟩=∫h dμ(T,β∧ω).                              (6)
T has even total degree. If β∧T=0, evaluate on fω for every smooth scalar f. Uniqueness forces μ(T,β∧ω)=0 and thus β∧(hT)=0. For a smooth scalar a, uniqueness gives μ(T,aθ)=a μ(T,θ), hence a(hT)=(ah)T. If C=γ∧T is positive, its coefficient measure equals μ(T,γ∧ω), so
hC=γ∧(hT).                                               (7)
For continuous a≥0 the same argument with positive aT gives h(aT)=(ha)T. No continuous wedge on an arbitrary signed current is invented.

For any current S and smooth β of total degree b, signed transposition gives
d(β∧S)=dβ∧S+(-1)^b β∧dS, d=d',d''.
Indeed commuting β past a total-degree-m current gives (-1)^{bm}; transposing differentiation gives (-1)^{m+b+1}; expanding d(β∧ω) on each compact test yields exactly those signs. This is the correctly indexed CLD7.7.7 calculation and assumes no closedness of S. For a smooth (k,k)-form γ the full second derivative is
D(γ∧S)=Dγ∧S-d''γ∧d'S+d'γ∧d''S+γ∧DS.                    (8)

Suppose T and C=γ∧T are both doubly closed. First-order Leibniz gives d'γ∧T=d''γ∧T=0. Differentiating the second relation gives Dγ∧T=0. For S=hT, the measure argument inherits ALL THREE annihilators. Differentiate d'γ∧S=0 by d'' and d''γ∧S=0 by d'; the form factors have odd total degree, giving
0=-Dγ∧S-d'γ∧d''S,
0=Dγ∧S-d''γ∧d'S.
Both cross terms in (8), and its Dγ term, therefore vanish. Thus
D(γ∧(hT))=γ∧D(hT).                                      (9)
The calculation explicitly allows hT to be nonclosed. For a scalar a it reads D((ah)T)=aD(hT), provided aT is doubly closed.

Consequently, for initial BT T, the actual smooth-factor product C=γ∧T is BT exactly when it is positive and doubly closed. Necessity is part of the definition. For sufficiency restrict to arbitrary ordinary O, take an admissible pair, and combine initial D(hT)=0 with (7) and (9). γ itself need be neither positive nor closed. Its actual product must be positive; closedness means precisely d'γ∧T=d''γ∧T=0. Require p+k≤n; for the nontrivial original degree range require p+k≤n-1. Degree n has no Hessian tests. Smooth a≥0 is allowable exactly when aT is doubly closed.

Fixed-T scalar nets: if locally smooth a_i≥0 converge locally uniformly to continuous a, and EVERY a_iT is doubly closed for the FIXED initial BT T, then aT is positive and closed by n1's measure convergence and transposition. For an admissible h on an arbitrary ordinary subopen and compact detector ω,
⟨D((a_i-a)hT),ω⟩=∫(a_i-a)h dμ(T,Dω)→0,
because the measure is finite and h bounded on its compact support. Each approximating BT identity is zero; locality completes the every-open conclusion. Arbitrary scalar smoothing supplies none of the required closedness equations.

Common-chart form nets: suppose every smooth γ_i∧T is positive and doubly closed, and γ_i converges in coefficients on compact supports in a FIXED finite family of common moment charts to a SMOOTH γ. Localize each test and expand in finite exterior monomial bases. Each monomial times the localized test has a fixed finite signed coefficient measure of T. Uniform coefficient convergence gives weak convergence of the products. Apply the same argument to d'ω and d''ω to get closedness; use positive tests for positivity. For BT apply it to Dω with the fixed bounded scalar h, then use (7). This constructs no nonsmooth wedge, changing-chart theorem, or arbitrary-current density.

The closedness diagnostic is an actual analytic example. Let X=(G_m,Q_ell²)^an, s_i=-log|T_i|, and a=2+s_1². X is good separated strict boundaryless pure dimension2. Its δ_X is positive doubly closed and tautologically BT. Nevertheless
D(aδ_X)=[2d's_1∧d''s_1].
For nonzero ζ≥0 smooth compact on R², ω=ζ(s)d's_2∧d''s_2 is an actual compact smooth upstairs test: its support lies in a compact closed analytic polyannulus. The identity moment has finite-flat degree1; CLD14.3.1–5,14.5.2–3 and5.8.4 give standard calibration and paired positive orientation. Hence
⟨D(aδ_X),ω⟩=2∫_{R²}ζ(s) ds_1 ds_2>0.
Thus aδ_X is INELIGIBLE as an original P21.3 current. This diagnoses the missing closedness premise in literal CLD8.6.7; it is not an original counterexample. Conversely S=(d's_1∧d''s_1)∧δ_X is positive closed BT, and d'a∧S=d''a∧S=0 by repeated generators, so aS is closed BT. Nonconstant relative weights are allowed.

The entire scalar367 and relative368 statement chains are reconstructed after replacing their unsupported strong-cone steps with n1's middle-cone construction. The repaired whole372 chain retains initial BT, actual product positivity/double closedness, every approximant's equations, and the smooth common-chart form limit. CLD8.5.5's generated-CPsh proof is not substituted for full original psh recognition; no arbitrary-current exhaustion follows from the printed closure propositions.

notes.summary: Analytic-trace removability holds in every original degree under explicit off-locus regularity and local smooth harmonic trace; whole372 conditional chain reconstructed, original P21.3 unresolved.
notes.detailedSummary: Constructs logarithmic cutoffs with exact inactive-variable omission, capped concave potentials with mass≤4LM and energy≤24L²M, genuine refined-unit-chart middle block bounds, and moving cutoff masses≤C(F+28M). Trace continuity gives vanishing, including r=0. Also proves an off-locus harmonic-approximation extension, isolated-point consequence, and constructed saturated-torus convolution sector. The independent conditional verdict is separate from the unresolved original universal assertion; candidate=false.
notes.text:
The reconstructed partial theorem is this. Work in n1's original ambient category. Let Z⊂W be ordinary closed and locally Zariski closed in analytic domains. Suppose h∈C(W,R) is ordinary smooth with Dh=0 on W\Z. Suppose every point of Z has an ordinary neighborhood N carrying an ordinary smooth g with Dg=0 and h=g on Z∩N. Then D(hT)=0 for EVERY positive doubly closed ordinary (p,p)-current, 0≤p≤n-1. There is no dimension restriction and no assumed cutoff-mass bound. The conclusion also holds if off Z smooth harmonicity is replaced by local uniform-on-compact approximation by ordinary smooth zero-Hessian functions: n1 proves exactly the same defect-support premise. This extension retains substantial additional hypotheses and does not close original P21.3.

Here is the complete cutoff construction. Localize in an affinoid neighborhood and choose a relatively compact ordinary subopen N carrying g. The locally analytic-locus description and affinoid noetherianity provide finitely many analytic f_1,…,f_m with common zero set Z∩N. Choose a real A at least two above their finite logarithmic upper bounds. Real constants require no nontrivial field scaling.

Let R_m be convolution of max(s_1,…,s_m) with a product of nonnegative smooth probability kernels supported in [-1/4,1/4]. It is smooth convex, translation-equivariant in the all-ones direction, and within1/4 of the maximum. If s_i is at least1 below the largest other coordinate, it cannot attain the maximum after any kernel translation: the gap remains at least1/2. Integrating out that coordinate omits it EXACTLY. Repeated omission allows coordinates -∞. Near a zero of one f_i outside the common zero locus, that coordinate is inactive; the remaining active f_i become ACTUAL analytic units after ordinary shrinking.

Off Z define t=A-R_m(log|f_1|,…,log|f_m|). CLD15.1.1–2 makes it ordinary smooth on these actual unit-moment charts. Its smooth Hessian is nonpositive because logarithmic-unit coordinates are affine and R_m has PSD Hessian. We have t≥0 and t→+∞ at Z. The exponentiated regularized maximum is continuous and vanishes exactly on the common zero locus. These are ordinary-topology assertions; no logarithmic chart crosses a zero.

Choose smooth nondecreasing concave b:[0,∞)→[0,4], equal to the identity on [0,2] and constant after4. Integrate a smooth nonincreasing derivative equal to1 up to2 and0 after4. Set u_L=L b(t/L), L≥1, giving it its constant capped value on Z. For fixed L it is constant on an ordinary neighborhood of Z, hence ordinary smooth on all N, including components contained in Z. The chain rule gives
0≤u_L≤4L, Du_L≤0, u_L=t when t≤2L.                         (10)

Fix compact symmetric (r,r)-test α and K=supp α. Take finitely many ordinary unit-moment charts U_j⊂N presenting α with coordinates s_j. Refine so that symmetrized smooth ambient representatives and their derivatives are defined near the relevant compact coordinate images. This follows from the local paralin definition and compactness. Choose compact subsets with interiors covering K, and 0≤ρ_j≤1 compact smooth in U_j and equal to1 near those subsets. Every point of K thus has some ρ_j=1 on a neighborhood. No global moment or global presentation is assumed.

Set λ_j=Σ_a d's_{j,a}∧d''s_{j,a} and η_j=λ_j^r, with η_j=1 for r=0. They are smooth positive doubly closed forms on U_j. Analytic pullbacks may be degenerate: domination is proved first in genuine ambient coefficient spaces. Define finite constants
M_j=|μ(T|U_j,Dρ_j∧η_j)|(U_j), F_j=⟨T|U_j,ρ_jλ_j^q⟩,
M=Σ_jM_j, F=Σ_jF_j.
All measures exist by n1. Expressions carrying ρ_j extend by zero to the SAME N.

Define nonnegative quantities
K_{j,L}=⟨T,ρ_j(-Du_L)∧η_j⟩,
E_{j,L}=⟨T,ρ_j d'u_L∧d''u_L∧η_j⟩.
The actual smooth-factor current T|U_j∧η_j is positive doubly closed by ordinary Leibniz; no initial BT premise is required. Closed-current smooth duality and (10) give
K_{j,L}=-⟨u_LT,Dρ_j∧η_j⟩≤4LM_j.                          (11)
Since D(u_L²)=2u_LDu_L+2d'u_L∧d''u_L,
2E_{j,L}=⟨u_L²T,Dρ_j∧η_j⟩-2⟨T,ρ_ju_LDu_L∧η_j⟩
≤16L²M_j+8LK_{j,L}≤48L²M_j.                              (12)
Thus K_L=ΣK_{j,L}≤4LM and E_L=ΣE_{j,L}≤24L²M. These estimates arise from FIXED finite signed measures, not unexplained uniform bounds for changing tests.

Choose smooth nondecreasing θ, zero on (-∞,1] and one on [2,∞). Set v_L=θ(t/L), σ_L=θ(2t/L), extended as1 on Z. Constancy near Z makes them ordinary smooth. Take a compact plateau ρ_*=1 near K and χ_L=ρ_*v_L. It equals1 near Z∩K. Plateau derivatives miss K, so
β_L=D(χ_Lα)=D(v_Lα)
=v_LDα+d'v_L∧d''α-d''v_L∧d'α+Dv_L∧α.                     (13)
β_L is compact in K and zero where t≤L. Derivatives of v_L occur only on L≤t≤2L, where u_L=t, and
Dv_L=L^-1 θ'(t/L)Dt+L^-2 θ''(t/L)d't∧d''t.

The required domination uses MIDDLE forms. On each U_j all coefficients of α,Dα,d'α,d''α in the chosen ambient representative are bounded on the compact image of supp ρ_j. Matrix order units give both-sign bounds by Cλ_j^r for α and Cλ_j^q for Dα. A degree exceeding the actual coordinate dimension has zero exterior coefficient space. No moment-coordinate dimension is inferred from n.

For the symmetric first-derivative cross term append a FORMAL independent covector dy to the old coefficient space, solely for linear algebra. Its q-th exterior space splits into old q-vectors and dy wedged with old r-vectors. The cross terms are off-diagonal blocks between these summands. For a bounded block A_j,
2|⟨A_jv,w⟩|≤C(|v|²+|w|²).
Rescaling the new component by L^-1 bounds both signs by
C(λ_j^q+L^-2 d't∧d''t∧λ_j^r).
Fixed positive factorial constants are absorbed in C.

Formal y is NOT asserted to be an analytic unit or moment coordinate. At each actual transition-region point, inactive-variable omission supplies actual active units f_i. Append those units to the old moment, obtaining a genuine refined chart in which t=τ(z). On each cell the FIRST-JET linear map sends old covectors to their old-coordinate projections and dy to dτ(z), identically on primed and double-primed copies.
